notes: GET /user returns a numeric id and a login. Its email field is null unless the token has user:email, so /login is the reviewed account label and /email is never used.
The owner and the repository are both written in the reviewed source, so only an issue number is selected per call. GitHub documents issue_number as a required integer path parameter.

On an issue, number, title, state and html_url are documented as required; body and state_reason are documented as string or null, and GitHub documents that blank fields are included as null instead of being omitted, so both are returned as explicit nulls.
The singular assignee field is not selected: it is being removed in the current documented API version, while the assignees array is only optionally present.

GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{issue_number} documents 200, 301, 304, 404 and 410. A transferred issue answers 301, an issue the token cannot read answers 404, and a deleted issue answers 410; Steed follows no redirect and treats each of those as a failure.

The same route documents that a pull request can be returned at the selected issue number, using the optional pull_request discriminator. read_issue does not select it, so a pull request projects to the same six fields and the read does not establish the object type.
POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues accepts title as required and body as an optional string; the reviewed profile sends only those two fields.
GitHub documents an unversioned default REST API version. Steed does not pin a version header, so behaviour follows GitHub's current documented default.

/repos/fixture-owner/fixture-repo/issues.title: Documented pull request returned by the issues route

secondary_rate_limit.documented: GitHub returns 403 with a documented message when a secondary rate limit is hit, and 429 for a primary limit.

revoked_token.documented: An expired, revoked or malformed token returns 401 Bad credentials.

wrong_owner.documented: A repository that is missing, or not visible to the token's repository selection, returns 404 rather than 403.

token_lifetime.documented: A fine-grained token's expiry is configurable: the documented expires_in value is an integer between 1 and 366 days, or none for a non-expiring token, defaulting to 30 days or less under an organization lifetime policy.
